newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to propose fining Germany and Italy.
newsitem.headline: EU to propose fining Germany and Italy.

text.p: The European Commission is set to propose on Wednesday fining Germany and Italy for ignoring EU court orders to apply environmental laws, Commission officials said on Tuesday.
"It shows that the Commission will use all the powers necessary to try to make member states comply with Community legislation," a Commission official said.
"You cannot take decisions like this easily. We are talking about a decision where the Community tells member states that they will have to pay a fine. That is pretty far-reaching," he added.
If the Commission agrees the fines, which would have to be confirmed by the Luxembourg-based court, it would be the first time it has used new powers granted in the Maastricht treaty, he said.

Bonn has failed to follow court rulings on ground water, surface water and bird protection while Rome has ignored court orders to apply EU legislation on waste disposal in Campania and basic measures for radiation protection of people undergoing medical treatment.
Officials would not say how big any fines would be, a matter they said the Commission would decide on Wednesday.

Earlier this year, the Commission agreed a method for imposing fines on countries which ignored court rulings taking into account how rich a country is, its voting weight in setting the original law and the seriousness and duration of the infringement.
